speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Pipelines are used to convey large quantities of petroleum and flammable materials from one location to another, for example, from the jetty where petroleum and flammable materials are unloaded off tankers to storage tanks in oil refineries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This will help Members to better understand the amendments that we are making to the Fire Safety Act (FSA).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Most of the pipelines that convey petroleum and flammable materials are on Jurong Island, while some are on the mainland.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: When they are above ground, multiple pipelines run together in pipeline corridors, where they are supported on piperacks or pipetracks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Underground sections of pipelines do not lie on any piperack or pipetrack and are either supported by structures, such as concrete slabs, or run through service tunnels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It is important to ensure the safe conveyance of petroleum and flammable materials and for there to be quick and effective response to any incident involving pipelines.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As such, under the current Act, "pipeline owners" have to obtain a licence under the Act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The licensed "pipeline owners" have to adhere to safety standards in the design, construction and maintenance of the pipelines.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They also have to ensure that there is regular inspection and maintenance of the pipelines and put in place emergency response plans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In a pipeline corridor, one party manages the piperacks or pipetracks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: However, the multiple pipelines that run through a corridor usually serve different users and premises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As a result, there could be one corridor with multiple pipeline owners managing different pipelines within that corridor.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This has posed operational challenges for SCDF on the ground as they have to deal with multiple parties with their own maintenance regimes and emergency response protocols for multiple pipelines within one and the same corridor.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is not ideal from a safety standpoint as no single party will have oversight and responsibility for the safety of all the pipelines running together in that corridor.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: More critically, it may not be immediately clear at the onset of an incident, such as a fire or explosion, which licensee is responsible for responding to the incident.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This will impact the timeliness and effectiveness of incident response efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The appropriate licensee should be the owner or lessee of the piperacks or pipetracks, who has overview of the safety of all the pipelines within its corridor.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I earlier mentioned that pipelines can run both above ground and underground.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For a pipeline corridor that traverses between two premises, there may be some segments that lie above ground and other segments that lie underground with no piperacks and pipetracks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In such cases, the owner of the pipeline corridor will be licensed for the entire pipeline between the two premises, including the underground segments that lie in between.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Where the pipelines to be licensed run completely underground, there is no piperack or pipetrack.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Bill also makes a consequential amendment to the definition of "relevant pipeline" under section 2(1) of the Fire Safety Act, to clarify that there may not be a piperack or pipetrack at certain sections of a pipeline.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As a regional hub for oil and gas, Singapore is covered with submarine and land lines connecting areas, such as Pulau Bukom and Jurong Island, to the mainland.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Pipelines carrying flammable materials are exposed to high risks, including rupture and oil spillage.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Just last month, governors in a few American states declared a state of emergency after a pipeline carrying petroleum ruptured in central Alabama, spilling more than 300,000 gallons of fuel in an ecologically-sensitive area and causing fuel shortages.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is a reminder that we cannot be complacent and should enact legislative changes before accidents occur.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This Bill will ensure that we have single-piece accountability for the integrity of our pipelines.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This will mean more efficient decision-making during emergency responses.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The frequent usage of pipelines leads to the reduction of wall thickness, creating higher chances of wall rupture.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Thus, in the long-term, the integrity of pipelines would also be more secure if one party is liable to conduct inspections, maintenance, train operations, staff and other such responsibilities.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: How would the Ministry choose which party to license?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Have we also sought Page: 32 feedback from the companies about these proposed changes?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Would the entire pipe network be considered as a single pipe corridor, meaning there is only one owner, or would it be considered as multiple pipe corridors, meaning that there are a few owners held accountable?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is an important point to raise because the integrity of the entire pipe network is dependent on the integrity of the weakest pipe, and maintenance of the entire network needs to be consistent.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I raise this question simply to seek clarity on the definition in the Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I appreciate it is difficult to explain this question in words and, as such, I have provided the Senior Minister of State with a drawing illustrating this point.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I also needed that drawing to understand what was written here.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Thirdly, can the Minister share what are the commercial implications of this change?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Louis Ng asks what the commercial implications of this change might be.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This has largely been achieved since the pipeline licensing regime was put in place through the Fire Safety Act amendments in 2013.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This round of amendments clarifies the definition of "pipeline owner" in the Act, to ensure that the appropriate parties will be licensed.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: SCDF has been working closely with the "pipeline owners" who will be licensed following these amendments and the necessary measures are already largely in place today.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Ng also asked about SCDF's licensing approach to a pipeline network with multiple pipelines that branch out from a point of supply to separate destinations – whether the network would be licensed under one party or multiple parties.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Different corridors may, therefore, have different licensees, but every licensee is held to the same standards.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Under SCDF's regulatory framework, every "pipeline owner" has to meet SCDF's stipulated safety standards for the maintenance of their pipelines.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This ensures that there is both Page: 33 integrity and consistency in the maintenance efforts across the entire pipeline network.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In addition, the licensed "pipeline owners" are also required to put in place comprehensive emergency response plans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: When an incident occurs, the respective "pipeline owners" are responsible for the emergency response and mitigation efforts for the segments of pipelines for which they have been licensed.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Should an incident occur at the boundary of two adjacent pipeline corridors, SCDF will activate both licensees for immediate emergency response.
